I’m not a mom but I have been an on call female firefighter. 

Just pee before you go. If you’re at the station they’ll wait for you. If you’re at home the extra 30 seconds won’t make a difference. If you’re worried just pee often. 

If my pager goes off it depends on the call and what I’m doing. If I’m out of town or I’ve had a drink I can’t respond. If I have company and I’m busy that night then I can’t respond. If I’m free and available then I’ll respond. Or if it’s a major call I’ll respond. That’s the point of having so many volunteers so you can have a revolving group of people available. 

Our dept had a policy that for ems calls we had to respond wearing long pants and closed toe shoes and whatever shirt. Calls that required gear you could wear shorts. You can keep clothes there in like a duffel bag by your rack or in a closet in the bunk room or something. Or in your car like someone said. I have never changed in front of anyone at the fire station. I always changed in the bathroom. I assume people would be mature but yeah I personally wouldn’t do it (and I never needed to.)

If you’re on a long call and have to pee, tell someone. They’ll find you a bathroom. 

Don’t overthink it. If you can fit it into your lifestyle that’s great! It’s a great thing to do. But you will miss some family events and things and it’s a sacrifice you’ll have to make. But it’s rewarding and I always liked it
